From d7a83d67a1694c42cc95fc0755d823f7ca3bfcfb Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Claudiu Beznea <claudiu.beznea@microchip.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Jan 2020 13:36:48 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] clk: at91: usb: use proper usbs_mask

Use usbs_mask passed as argument. The usbs_mask is different for
SAM9X60.

Fixes: 2423eeaead6f8 ("clk: at91: usb: Add sam9x60 support")
Signed-off-by: Claudiu Beznea <claudiu.beznea@microchip.com>
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/1579261009-4573-4-git-send-email-claudiu.beznea@microchip.com
Acked-by: Alexandre Belloni <alexandre.belloni@bootlin.com>
Signed-off-by: Stephen Boyd <sboyd@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/clk/at91/clk-usb.c b/drivers/clk/at91/clk-usb.c
index 3c0bd7e51b09..c0895c993cce 100644
--- a/drivers/clk/at91/clk-usb.c
+++ b/drivers/clk/at91/clk-usb.c
@@ -214,7 +214,7 @@ _at91sam9x5_clk_register_usb(struct regmap *regmap, const char *name,
 
 	usb->hw.init = &init;
 	usb->regmap = regmap;
-	usb->usbs_mask = SAM9X5_USBS_MASK;
+	usb->usbs_mask = usbs_mask;
 
 	hw = &usb->hw;
 	ret = clk_hw_register(NULL, &usb->hw);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/clk/at91/clk-usb.c`**
- The line that sets the `usbs_mask` for the USB clock structure has been modified. 
- The original line `usb->usbs_mask = SAM9X5_USBS_MASK;` has been changed to `usb->usbs_mask = usbs_mask;`, allowing the function to use the `usbs_mask` passed as an argument instead of a hardcoded value.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a specific issue related to the SAM9X60 platform, where the `usbs_mask` differs from that of the SAM9X5. By using the `usbs_mask` passed as an argument, the code becomes more flexible and correct for different hardware configurations. This change is a direct fix for the previously introduced support for SAM9X60, as indicated by the fix reference in the patch.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
usb->usbs_mask = SAM9X5_USBS_MASK;
```
Reason:
The hardcoded value `SAM9X5_USBS_MASK` is used for the `usbs_mask` in the USB clock registration function, which does not accommodate the different `usbs_mask` required for the SAM9X60 platform. This results in incorrect USB clock initialization for the SAM9X60.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
usb->usbs_mask = usbs_mask;
```
Reason:
By using the `usbs_mask` passed as an argument instead of a hardcoded value, the code now correctly utilizes the appropriate mask for the SAM9X60 platform, ensuring proper USB clock initialization.
